summary: Submitted the checker_correspondence review of the bootstrap check (artifact 7b46154414c54350ab9fe434a0b2e5f7), status no_issue_found with no open issues and no execution attribution (target test exited zero). The trusted runner executed the fixed harness in a clean copy: bootstrap_attempt recorded first_error true with the simulated StoreLog failure firing and log_index_after_first 0, and bootstrap_outcome recorded existing_state true, retry_allowed false, second_error 'bootstrap only works on new clusters' and log_index_after_retry 0, so P-retry-allowed was a complete violated witness whose only blocker was the missing correspondence review. The review establishes applicability (BootstrapCluster takes caller-supplied stores, the LogStore interface permits StoreLog to fail, and the harness starts from a store HasExistingState confirms is clean) and observation validity (the attempt event shows the failure actually fired; the outcome event carries the guard's answer, the retry error and the observed log index under the same identity label; retry_allowed is derived from the second attempt's own error plus the observed index rather than a scenario constant, and the zero index shows no configuration entry exists). It keeps the compared proposition separate from the wider consequence and explicitly does not claim that no recovery exists, since RecoverCluster is excluded and unexercised. Limitations preserve the scope: single simulated failure, production reachability unestablished, operator remedy excluded, local duty only. If accepted, this removes the sole blocker and should confirm the fifth in-scope violation; preflight returned valid:true against map v9, and the four earlier findings remain confirmed.
